steps.text: Mix cream cheese and butter together in a bowl until smooth.
Gradually stir in flour until just combined. Shape dough into a ball; cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 3 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).
Roll out dough on a floured pastry board to a thickness of 1/8 inch. Cut into 2 ½-inch squares and place about 1/2 teaspoon of jam or preserves in the center.
Overlap opposite corners and pinch together to seal. Place on ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden, about 10 to 12 minutes. Cool on wire racks. Dust kolacky lightly with confectioners sugar.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream Cheese Kolacky
raw_recipe.description: Kolacky are cream cheese pastries that you can fill with your favorite fruit jam. You may want to double this recipe — these holiday treats go fast!

video.description: These decadent cream cheese cookies filled with jam are delicious and easy to make! They win in presentation style too! Make these jam filled treats for your your next get together!

review.reviewBody: I have been making these delicious cookies for years and I found an easier way for me . I just roll them in small balls and make a thumbprint in them and fill and bake them ,when cooled I roll in powdered sugar, same great taste and much less work

truly great, truly simple. .chilled for about two hours and to simplify, I made a "log" and rolled it in plastic wrap; just sliced, dolloped and baked. No rolling or unnecessary handling. Baked about 15 minutes though. and

I've been making cream cheese Kolacky over 40 years and this recipe is perfect as is, however I make a much larger batch using a lb. of butter, lb. of cream cheese, 4 cups flour and a couple tsp. of vanilla. I also make a walnut filling instead of preserves by grinding a lb. of walnuts or pecans and mixing with 1 1/4 cups sugar and two beaten egg whites. Like another reviewer I also roll them out on a liberal dusting of powdered sugar in lieu of dusting them with it. It carmelizes the bottom and adds yet another tasty dimension to an already scrumptious cookie. These proportions make plenty to share for Christmas gifts, but I must warn you-you will be asked to make them every year!! :)

Jam, preserves, or pie filling won't work as well as a true fruit/nut pastry filling. Solo brand is excellent and never runs (unless you overfill). The recipe I use for the dough is 0.5 lb of butter and 0.5 lb of cream cheese with 2 cups of flour. If the dough is properly chilled, you don't need much extra flour to keep things from sticking. In years of making these pastries, the dough doesn't seem to suffer from a little extra flour - just don't over work/knead it to start or during the rolling out process.

A super simple, tried and true, crowd-pleasing recipe! This is my go-to, and I've got it down to a science: Make your life simple, like I have... Make the dough ahead of when you wish to bake. I mix up 8x the recipe at one sitting. Cut the butter and cream cheese together with the flour, then mix as little as possible with your hands; due to arthritis, I usually end up just 'knuckling' the dough in the bowl, to bring it all together. Next, form dough into fist-sized rough balls and roll each one between two sheets of wax-paper. Needless to say, Don't chill first! Roll them to the thickness you wish your cookies to be, so you don't have to roll later. Stack the rolled-out balls together on a pan (I use a pizza pan), wrap in plastic wrap and stash in fridge. When ready to make into cookies, remove dough from fridge one 'disk' at a time as you use them. Peel wax paper off one side to loosen, then replace, flip and peel off the other side. I use a pizza-slicer to cut the dough into squares and save the weird end pieces to re-roll when all 'disks' are used up. Put filling into plastic baggie and clip one corner off. Pipe filling in a diagonal onto dough squares, bring up opposite ends and pinch. Transfer to baking sheet and bake as directed. By piping the filling, my fingers stay clean and I am able to control how much filling I wish to use. It's not unusual for me to do a 'line' of cream-cheese filling alongside a fruit filling on the same cookie! Hubby love it and so do I.
I tried this recipe and I put Solo Almond filling instead of preserves. It knocked my husbands socks off.

Wow. I tasted the raw dough & it was not good at all. Put it in the freezer & did not have high hopes for a very good cookie. Let it thaw a little. Decided I was tired so I put powdered sugar in a large baggie, rolled dough into balls, threw them into the sugar, put the balls on a cookie sheet, smashed with my finger, added peach preserves to the middle of the cookie & wallaa . . . very tasty treat!

This cookie was DIVINE! It defintely needs the sugar or icing or it isn't sweet....... I sprinkled as I've seen some do with granulated sugar before baking. I used apricot preserves..... this is one of the best cookie recipes I've eaten...... very true to real kolacky...... the results are light and pastry like..... I think you could add a touch of vanilla...... this cookies is best NOT hot right out of the oven..... it is too hot and the buttery smell and flavor are overpowering..... these cookies are best next day or thrououghly cooled..... the cookie softens slightly in storage....

I have not made this version of kolacky. But I grew up with my mom making them every Christmas. It was a favorite in our family. I have been making them by her recipe ever since. But they are richer. 1, 1, and 1. Simple. Easy to remember. After, I read other posts here a few suggestions; she used an old Sunbeam stand mixer, then she would chill them in small rounds that way they would be easier to work with. They need to be chilled when rolling out. Don't let them "thaw". Cutting them on a diagonal then the other diagonal leaves diamonds if you want to roll them. ""Roll the dough out on confectionery sugar, NOT flour. Flour will make the dough drier and harder to work with."" CRUTAL: don't over cook, just until golden brown. Take it from a Batchelor who has done it. What a mess.🫣

I remembered these from my time decades ago working in a bakery. Couldn't remember what they were called, only the shape & that they were cream cheese based. Glad I found the recipe here. It was my first time making them; I was asked to make a dessert for an event I was not able to attend personally. I was very pleased with how they turned out. I was told they were a 'hit' & people kept asking repeatedly who made them and had to keep being told 'she's not here'. lol. My TIPS/TRICKS if you make these in the traditional shape: My bench/dough scraper was invaluable! I made a 2 1/2" square paper template, then used the bench scraper to press-cut the sections out (using a knife or similar to 'slice' ruined the dough edges). Make sure each is/stays a perfect SQUARE. If not, add rejects to the pile you will roll out again. Use scraper and make sure the dough section is NOT stuck to the work surface before adding the jam. Keep jam amount to 1/2 t or it will overflow. (I also mixed 1T of flour into jam to help prevent overflow as another reviewer recommended). If any corner isn't 'sharp' use this as one of the overlapping flaps to disguise it. Make sure to overlap EQUAL amounts of the two opposing corners, or it will still end up being mis-shapen (& make the overlap more than barely touching!) I used a q-tip and added a touch of water to help the flaps stay closed, as I lightly pinched them. If any flaps should still open while baking, just press it back down while it's still hot out of the oven. And yes, your arm will get somewhat of a workout stirring the ingredients together, as well as when you initially roll out the hard dough.

They were delicious!! The dough was so easy and came out so nice. Pastry part had the nicest tiniest rise and flaky'ness but not too much. I used filling from bakery and did happy of them apricot and other half of recipe with raspberry. When cutting out the dough i used a 2 3/4 inch circle, snipped a half inch off the tip of the fruit filling pastry bag, and did thick line of filling through center of dough circle, then folded each of the 2 sides over. They looked beautiful. I was surprised the recipe didn't make more cookies. I doubled the recipe, did the small circles, and the double recipe only made 44 cookies. But they were amazing. Thank you for this recipe.

I grew up in Chicago. All of the bakeries (i.e., German, Italian, French) had their own version of kolacky. My favorite was an Italian bakery across from where I lived in the city. Their version was very similar to this recipe, except instead of overlapping the dough, it was cut into circles and the top filled with fruit. That's how I do it now. I make these every Easter as a part of our Polish Easter.
These were pretty but dry and not sweet. My husband who likes pie crust said it was even too tasteless for him. I gave some to my sugar/baked goods addicted kid and she didn’t like them.
Thank you for the recipe! I will say my Grandma from Austria taught me to pinch the edges using just one hand- the thumb and pointer finger☺️ it helps to have flour on your fingers.

Don't overthink it! I followed the recipe. You only need to refrigerate the dough for 1 hour. I used Smuckers peach preserves as it is thicker and did not run. Moisten your fingers with water and pinch and fold the dough. 12 min bake time was perfect. Next time I will triple the recipe, they are amazing!!
Family favorite, passed down from my Czech family.

I’ve been making these for years using this exact same recipe with wonderful results. The secret to preventing them from coming out like pancakes is to refrigerate your tray of cookies right AFTER you’ve filled them. Put them in the fridge for at least 10-15 minutes. They will firm up really nice and not spread out when you bake them. Trust me! Yes it is time consuming but after all that work of rolling, cutting, & filling them you want them to turn out perfect and they will as long as you let them get cold & firm up.
Delish...... Just take the dough out of the fridge for an hour or 2.... it's Rock Hard! Had everything ready then....wow....can't roll out the dough!
